## Flash an older build, and the emulator stops lying to you

**Stuck in a boot loop? Roll back.** The flasher has a **firmware version** picker now, offering the two releases before this one. Pick one, flash it, and you're back on a build that worked.

It only appears when there's something to go back to, so from here on every release keeps its two predecessors flashable.

**The emulator now looks like the device.** It was showing you a sharper, larger picture than the thing you actually ship — single-pixel details that read as soft edges on a 2.4" panel came out as hard staircases in a browser, which made some sprites look wrong when they were fine on hardware.

There's a **panel** control with three settings — off, scanlines, pixel grid — and a **zoom** control from 1× to 4×, or fit. The overlay measures the real zoom and draws one line per actual device pixel, so it stays proportionally the same whether you're on a phone or at 4× on a desktop.

**Squachy's outline sticks to him now.** The keyline added last release was drawn once at his neutral pose, so the moment he walked or swayed his arms slid out from under their own outlines and left them hanging in space. Every limb now draws its own outline immediately before itself — including the moods that throw his arms out as wide lines at completely different angles, which a fixed outline could never have matched.

**Digital rain** loses the wind (it read as drift rather than weather) and gains a **CRT sweep**: one pass down the field every ten seconds, with a dark retrace gap ahead of a bright edge, which is what makes a roll bar legible on a black field instead of a haze. Drop colour is now tied to depth, so far drops run cool and near ones warm.

**The starfield tunnel rides the warp** — when the stars streak, the rings scroll and rotate with them, up to about 3.7×, so a burst accelerates the whole scene rather than the stars racing past a tube going its own pace.

**Mowin' Man works above the counters** instead of underneath them. The animated band runs behind the detection numbers, so standing him at the bottom of it put him under the readout.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: firmware version picker in the flasher, offering the previous two releases
- **Added**: LCD panel simulation and a zoom control in the emulator
- **Changed**: digital rain drops the wind, gains a CRT sweep, and couples hue to depth
- **Changed**: the starfield tunnel accelerates with the warp
- **Fixed**: Squachy's outline stayed at his neutral pose while his limbs moved
- **Fixed**: Mowin' Man mowed underneath the detection counters

Everything in this release is drawing code — nothing touches detection, boot or hardware setup.
